developer_request: AAOP: take over this project. I cannot develop software, do not know where it is now, and do not know what should happen next.
known_facts: The owner has delegated ordinary development responsibility but supplied no roadmap or current task.
The repository contains project instructions, current implementation, tests, CI signals, history, and possibly stale continuity artifacts that can recover much of the intent and baseline.
Existing AAOP Working Contract, Journey, discovery, Routes, verification, and provider-selection mechanisms already exist; the missing behavior is their default autonomous composition.
A technical uncertainty, failing test, unfamiliar architecture, or missing task list is not a product decision owned by the novice.
expected_first_moves: reconcile governing instructions, current repository/runtime evidence, Working Contract, and any Journey checkpoint before trusting old plans or status files
reconstruct ultimate intent from authoritative project evidence and distinguish it from the current development goal
select the highest-value evidence-backed safe next delta without asking the owner to choose a route, roadmap, stack, provider, or task
implement and verify the smallest coherent delta, then re-read current evidence and continue the next-delta loop while an authorized delta exists
must_preserve: AAOP authority over Working Contract, Journey, Route, authorization, acceptance, and handoff
host-native first and existing project capability before provider escalation
project-specific product authority and explicit completion/target-evidence boundaries
the distinction between a route-level verified no-op and long-horizon Journey completion
must_not: stop at repository analysis, a roadmap, a handoff document, or one completed delta when current evidence supports another safe next delta
make the novice supply a technical plan, stack choice, route, provider, test strategy, or ordinary debugging decision
treat ordinary technical uncertainty as a human-owned blocker or as justification for a default provider
invent product intent when a material value fork cannot be recovered from evidence or a safe experiment
add a duplicate planner, workflow engine, state database, or execution runtime
lessons: A default takeover is a composition of existing AAOP control surfaces, not a new orchestration product.
Ultimate intent and the current development goal must be reconstructed separately so an owner does not have to schedule the work.
Autonomy means continuing across verified deltas while preserving genuine human and production boundaries.
